newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices recover but still below week's high.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices recover but still below week's high.

text.p: Oil prices ended a wildly volatile week with a $1.00 per barrel rally on Friday, but still failed to make up all the ground lost in a ferocious mid-week selloff sparked by the resumption of Iraqi oil exports.
January futures for world benchmark Brent Blend crude closed up $1.03 at $23.55 per barrel.
The futures price has gained about $1.50 per barrel since Thursday, but ended the week about 70 cents below Monday's high.
Some market analysts said big moves reflected market nervousness over conflicting factors of cold weather on the bullish side, and the resumption of Iraqi crude exports, on the bearish.
Others pointed to "big money" investment fund speculators who took profits on existing long positions early in the week after a sustained rally, and then re-established new longs on Friday.
"It's a thin market, so if the funds come in and need to do some business, it pushes the market around," a London futures broker said.
Iraqi oil flowed into the market for the first time since 1990 when Baghdad was hit by a United Nations' trade ban after it invaded Kuwait.
After months of wrangling between Baghdad and the U.N., a plan allowing Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to pay for food and medicines got the green light.
Although only a handful of contracts have been signed, traders reckon Iraq will eventually ship about 500,000-600,000 barrels of oil daily to the market.
Forecasts for colder weather in some parts of the United States, the world's largest heating oil consumer, provided some bullish impetus on Friday, traders said.
Though there has been some stock building in recent weeks as refineries work overtime to build supplies before bitter weather hits, U.S. inventories remain below 1995 levels.
